name: Keyphrase Extraction Large-Scale Evaluation
description: Keyphrase extraction models are usually evaluated under different, not directly comparable, experimental setups. As a result, it remains unclear how well proposed models actually perform, and how they compare to each other. In this work, we address this issue by presenting a systematic large-scale analysis of state-of-the-art keyphrase extraction models involving multiple benchmark datasets from various sources and domains. Our main results reveal that state-of-the-art models are in fact still challenged by simple baselines on some datasets. We also present new insights about the impact of using author- or reader-assigned keyphrases as a proxy for gold standard, and give recommendations for strong baselines and reliable benchmark datasets.
evaluation_method: F1-based metrics (precision/recall/F1, commonly reported as F1@k or F1@M for top-k predictions)
notes: Heterogeneous benchmark combining many datasets and domains; gold standards vary (author-assigned vs reader-assigned) which affects comparability; evaluation depends on matching/normalization choices—care needed when comparing results.
